page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top left ("LIBER IIII."), page number at top right (297). No marginal notes. Signature at bottom right ("T 5"). A decorative ornament in the left margin is not text.

main_text.p: torum impetus nauis iactatione efficiat, medióque interposito, Aestus maris: facilè concludetur, quod medio adhærescit, ei quoque cui medium conuenit, necessariò conuenire.
main_text.head: CAP. IIII.
main_text.p: VOT funt Medij collocandi formæ? Tres. Nam aut inter duos quæstionis terminos interponitur, qui locus Medio maximè conuenit: aut supra utrunque, aut sub utroque. unde tres Syllogismi figuræ ab Aristotele factæ sunt: prima ex loco Medij dignisimo: secunda ex eo qui minus dignus est: tertia ex infimo.

Quomodo medium inter utrunque extremum interiicitur? Cum primo loco maius extremum de ipso dicitur: pòst ipsum de minore. Nam propositio fit ex medio & attributo: assumptio ex subiecto & medio. unde subiecti & attributi cōuenientia perspicitur. Scitum est autem, quod Aristoteles scribit, ex figuris omnibus hanc esse ad docendum accommodatissimā, & mathematicas omnes scientias, veluti Arithmeticā, & Geometriam, suas in hac figura demōstrationes concludere: propterea quòd omnes quæ caussa rei fit, declarant. certissimum autem & exquisitissimū sci-endi genus esse, per quod rei cuiusque caussa intelligitur.

page.notes: Printing errors left as printed: "dignisimo" (for dignissimo), "caussa" as printed with double long s. The word "sci-endi" at the line break is doubtful, read as "sciendi" with the hyphen at the break. The opening word of the chapter is set in small capitals ("VOT"); the initial letter is uncertain and may be Q ("Quot"), so it is copied as printed. The "&" forms are ligatures and are copied as "&" where they appear as the Latin ampersand. The "ct" ligature in "iactatione" is read as printed.
